Topic: Kul Devta — Why Worshipping Your Family Deity Comes First, and the Cosmic Hierar chy Behind It

Sour ce: A short Ashaeiynn Foundation training video (video transcript, ~14 min) — a dir ect instructional monologue rather than a live satsang Q&A, with no audience questions or back-and-forth pr esent in the sour ce material. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on conversational content: this is a short, dir ect training monologue with no sangat backand-forth — ther e is no separate curated conversational supplement for this session (see closing note).
1. WHY THIS TOPIC MATTERS

This session opens with a dir ect statement: worship (aaradhana) of one's Kul Devta (family/ancestral deity) is essential. The Kul Devta is described as "the father of the household" — and this teaching frames proper Kul Devta worship as a genuine prerequisite standing before any other spiritual progress becomes possible.
2. KUL DEVTA WORSHIP AS A PREREQUISITE FOR EVERYTHING ELSE

Ashaeiynn has practitioners worship their own Kul Devta alongside Hanuman Ji Maharaj specifically because, without the Kul Devta's permission, Hanuman Ji Maharaj will not enter a person's home. Only with the Kul Devta's permission can a practitioner genuinely awaken bhagwan's (God's) shakti at all. Without the Kul Devta's grace and power , a practitioner cannot awaken their drishti (spiritual sight) even if they deeply wish to — this teaching states plainly that every drishti awakened at Ashaeiynn has depended on Kul Devta grace, without exception.
3. KUL DEVTA IS NOT THE SAME THING AS A PITRU

A crucial distinction: pitrus (deceased family members) never become Kul Devtas. Pitrus ar e simply those among a family's own lineage who have died — no matter how powerful a pitru becomes, it cannot take on the form or position of a devta. If a pitru genuinely became a devta, it would, by definition, no longer be a pitru at all — the two categories ar e mutually exclusive.
4. WHERE A KUL DEVTA'S SHAKTI ORIGINATES

Every lineage (kul) has, at some point in its history , a particular ancestor who founded that lineage — and it is thr ough that founding, in each case, that a specific Kul Devi's or Kul Devta's shakti was originally awakened for that family line.
5. THE COSMIC HIERARCHY: THE FORMLESS SUPREME BRAHMAN BEHIND EVERYTHING

This teaching places a formless Parabrahma Parameshwar (Supreme Divine Reality) — r eferred to variously as Bhagwan Ram, Sadashiva, or Nirakar Parabrahma (the formless Supr eme) — as distinct fr om and beyond all specific deities. Numerous shaktis (divine powers) ar e described as having taken avatar (incarnate form) specifically in order to awaken and manifest aspects of that ultimate, formless r eality .
6. EVEN THE MOTHER GODDESS WAS ONCE HUMAN

This teaching r eveals that Maha Maai (the Mother Goddess widely worshipped as Mata) was, at some point in time, herself in human form. Through her own tapasya (austerity) and spiritual attainment, she pr ogr essively gr ew in statur e, drawing cosmic energy fr om beyond Parabrahma itself into a saakar (embodied, form-based) manifestation — this is offer ed as the underlying r eason the Mata form is worshipped at all, rather than practitioners going dir ectly to the formless Parabrahma itself.
7. BHAGW AN SHIVA AS "MAHAGURU" — THE SERVICE-STATION ANALOGY

Bhagwan Shiva likewise began, in this teaching's account, as a person named Shankar , who awakened what this teaching calls "Shiv tattva" (the Shiva element/essence) — a genuinely awakened, living principle, illustrated by an account of visiting Kailash and witnessing countless (anginat) forms of Bholenath ther e simultaneously . Having awakened Shiv tattva, Bhagwan Shiva dr ew cosmic energy fr om the wider universe and gave it a saakar (embodied) form, which he then distributes downward to others — this is why he is called "Mahaguru" (the gr eat teacher) and "Devon ke Dev Mahadev" (God of gods). A concr ete analogy is offer ed: Bhagwan Shiva effectively opened a "service station" — if a person needs "air for their tires" (a specific blessing or boon), they can simply visit that service station rather than needing to build an entir ely separate compr essor system (i.e., undertaking the complete tapasya themselves fr om scratch).
8. EVER Y DEVI-DEVTA WAS ONCE HUMAN AND UNDERWENT (OFTEN UNKNOWN) TAPASYA

This teaching generalizes the pattern: every devi and devta was, at some point, a human being who undertook tapasya, awakened specific tattvas/shaktis, and r ose to their current divine statur e and dimension — meaning each is simultaneously human, devta, and divine, having personally experienced the full range fr om the bottom to the top. A specific example is given fr om within this teaching's own lineage: Baba Ramdev Peer (Ashaeiynn's own Kul Devta, as referenced in this teaching) performed 12 years of tapasya at a single location, despite alr eady being an avatar of Vishnu — no one, including this teaching's own tradition, knows pr ecisely why that additional tapasya was necessary . Similarly , no one knows the specifics of how much tapasya Bhagwan Ganesh, Adi Shakti Mata, or Bholenath individually performed to r each their current statur e — the pattern nonetheless applies to all of them.
9. WHY MATA IS CONSIDERED THE MOST POWERFUL — SHE IS THE OLDEST

This teaching states that Mata (the primordial goddess) is the oldest of these divine figur es, and it is specifically her seniority/antiquity that makes her the most powerful. Bhagwan Ram is described as having come later , and Bholenath similarly emerged afterward — establishing a rough chronological hierarchy among these figures based on when each rose to their current stature.
10. DEVI-DEVT AS AS "BRANCHES" DISTRIBUTING PARABRAHMA'S ENERGY

The devi-devtas function, in this teaching's framing, as channels or "branches" (Bhagwan Shiva's own "service stations," so to speak) thr ough which Parabrahma Parameshwar's underlying energy gets distributed downward to ordinary people. A particular Kul Devta, in turn, r epresents one further branch specific to a given family lineage — being born into that lineage means a person is automatically , structurally connected to that specific devta's channel.
1 1. WHY INDEPENDENTLY CHOOSING TO WORSHIP AN UNRELATED DEITY DOESN'T WORK AS WELL

This teaching dir ectly cautions against the attitude of dismissing one's own lineage-based devta in favor of independently choosing to worship a differ ent deity of personal pr eference (the example given: "I'll worship Bhagwan Krishna in my own way instead"). The stated r easoning: if a person wants that specific power without going thr ough the established, structural channel (their own Kul Devta), they would effectively need to build an entir ely separate channel of their own — meaning r epeating the full tapasya that a figur e like Bhagwan Shiva originally performed to establish that channel in the first place. This teaching bluntly states that attempting this shortcut instead typically leads to a person's own undoing ("tumhara nipata ho jayega").
12. WHY VISITING MANY DIFFERENT TEMPLES ONLY YIELDS "ALMS" (BHEEK)

Visiting many differ ent dhams (shrines) and temples, seeking blessings her e and ther e without a pr operly established personal channel, is described in this teaching as r eceiving mer e "bheek" (alms/charity) rather than genuine, full access — a person will r eceive only as much as would typically be given as alms, and nothing beyond that limited amount.
13. THE THREE-TIER STRUCTURE WITHIN ASHAEIYNN'S PRACTICE

Within Ashaeiynn's specific practice structur e: the Kul Devta is worshipped as a father figur e, Hanuman Ji Maharaj is worshipped as Ishta Devta (a personally chosen worshipped deity), and Gurudev (r eferring to the guiding spiritual authority within Ashaeiynn) is also tr eated with the same r ever ence as a Kul Devta figur e. Each family/lineage carries a specific devta's shakti running thr ough it, and that shakti's r ole in bringing higher power down to the practitioner is described as genuinely significant.
14. WHY THIS TEACHING IS BEING SURFACED NOW

This teaching frames itself as something Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself has taken specific r esponsibility ("theka utha liya hai") for making known to everyone — with the teacher's own r ole described modestly as simply following instructions ("bhagwan/guru ne bola, hum karte hain") rather than personal initiative. The stated r eason this specific teaching matters practically: a person's own personal shakti cannot be pr operly established in their home until their Kul Devta has first been pr operly established ther e.
15. WHY DIRECTLY WORSHIPPING ISHTA DEVTA WITHOUT ESTABLISHING KUL DEVTA CAN BACKFIRE

This teaching warns that attempting to worship one's Ishta Devta (or a higher power) dir ectly , without first pr operly establishing one's Kul Devta, risks a practitioner becoming genuinely "trapped" (fas jaoge). The reason given: a

person's own pitrus (ancestral spirits) stand between them and that higher power , and a pitru will effectively inter cept the practitioner's jaap for itself ("tu side mein ho na, tera jaap main lunga") befor e it ever reaches its intended destination.
16. WHY EVEN REACHING ONE'S OWN KUL DEVTA CAN TAKE A LONG TIME

Even r eaching one's own Kul Devta — despite this being the mor e accessible, appr opriate channel compar ed to attempting a dir ect appr oach to a higher power — can take considerable time, because a practitioner's own generational line of ancestral pitrus stands ahead of them, one after another . A concr ete family analogy is used: imagine a gr eat-grandfather is present, followed in sequence by his sons, then their sons, and so on — the youngest, most r ecently born family member's own "turn" would come last in that queue. If that youngest member tries to step forward and r each the gr eat-grandfather directly , the many people standing ahead in that generational queue would naturally ask what business the youngest one has jumping ahead — until a genuine bond/connection is established with those ahead in the queue, the youngest member simply won't be let thr ough easily , even though, once genuine closeness is established, that youngest member would typically become the most doted-upon ("sabse zyada laad") family member of all.
17. HOW ASHAEIYNN'S SHAKTIS HELP CLEAR THIS QUEUE

This teaching states that Ashaeiynn's own shaktis can be used to help clear this generational "queue" of ancestral pitrus, ensuring that a practitioner's bhog (ritual offerings) genuinely r each their intended Kul Devta rather than being intercepted along the way . Many practitioners do not even know who their own Kul Devta actually is — yet thr ough consistent deepak (lamp) offering practice alone, Hanuman Ji Maharaj is described as dir ectly r evealing and naming each individual practitioner's specific Kul Devta over time, entirely without any special power on the teacher's own part being required. Ashaeiynn teaches the pr oper vidhi (ritual method/pr ocedur e) for corr ectly acquiring a Kul Devta's grace, and for ensuring that a practitioner's r elationship with their Kul Devta genuinely deepens over time — deepak practice alone will produce gradual progress, but this teaching notes that hawan (fire ritual) carries its own distinct, more intense "taap" (heat/potency) compared to deepak practice.
18. HA WAN AS A STRONGER ALTERNATIVE, INDIVIDUALLY PRESCRIBED

For practitioners whose ongoing pitru-r elated pr oblems make consistent Kul Devta worship difficult, hawan is offer ed as a str onger , faster alternative method, with the specific bhog first being conveyed to the Kul Devta thr ough the guru's own mediation. The exact number of hawans pr escribed varies fr om person to person, based entir ely on the guru's own individual assessment — someone already carrying substantial prior grace may be prescribed relatively few hawans, while someone else may be prescribed more, depending entirely on their specific individual circumstances.

Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 28, English)
Kul Devta — Why Worshipping Your Family Deity Comes First, and the Cosmic Hierar chy Behind It
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation training module. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Why does Ashaeiynn insist on worshipping my Kul Devta alongside Hanuman Ji Maharaj? A: Jai Siya Ram! Because the Kul Devta is described as "the father of the household," and without their permission, Hanuman Ji Maharaj will not enter a person's home. Without the Kul Devta's permission, a practitioner cannot genuinely awaken bhagwan's shakti at all — and every drishti awakened at Ashaeiynn has depended on Kul Devta grace, without exception.

Q2. Is my Kul Devta the same as my deceased ancestors (pitrus)? A: No — this is an important distinction. Pitrus are simply deceased family members, and no matter how powerful a pitru becomes, it can never take on the form or position of a devta. If a pitru genuinely became a devta, it would, by definition, no longer be a pitru at all.

Q3. Where does a Kul Devta's power actually come fr om? A: Every lineage (kul) has a particular ancestor at some point in its history who founded that lineage, and it is through that founding that the family's specific Kul Devi's or Kul Devta's shakti was originally awakened.

Q4. Is ther e something even higher than all the gods and goddesses I know about? A: Yes — this teaching describes a formless Parabrahma Parameshwar (referred to variously as Bhagwan Ram, Sadashiva, or Nirakar Parabrahma) as distinct from and beyond all specific deities. Numerous divine powers took avatar specifically to awaken and manifest aspects of that ultimate, formless reality .

Q5. Was the Mother Goddess (Mata) always divine, or did she become that way? A: Per this teaching, Maha Maai was at one point herself in human form. Through her own tapasya and spiritual attainment, she progressively grew in stature, eventually drawing cosmic ener gy from beyond Parabrahma itself into an embodied (saakar) form — this is why the Mata form is worshipped, rather than practitioners approaching the formless Parabrahma directly .

Q6. Was Lord Shiva always a fully divine being too? A: This teaching describes Bhagwan Shiva as having begun as a person named Shankar , who awakened "Shiv tattva" — a genuinely living, awakened principle (illustrated by an account of witnessing countless forms of Bholenath simultaneously at Kailash). He then drew cosmic ener gy and gave it embodied form, distributing it downward — which is why he's called Mahaguru and "Devon ke Dev Mahadev ."

Q7. What's the "service station" analogy about Lord Shiva? A: This teaching describes Bhagwan Shiva as having ef fectively opened a "service station" for cosmic ener gy — if you need something specific (like "air for your tires"), you can simply go to that service station rather than building your own entire compressor system, meaning undertaking the complete tapasya yourself from scratch to access that same power independently .

Q8. Did every god and goddess go thr ough some kind of spiritual struggle to r each their current status? A: Yes — this teaching's general pattern is that every devi and devta was once a human being who performed tapasya, awakened specific tattvas/shaktis, and

rose to their current stature. A specific example given is Baba Ramdev Peer performing 12 years of tapasya despite already being a Vishnu avatar — even this teaching's own tradition doesn't fully know why that additional tapasya was necessary .

Q9. Why is Mata consider ed mor e powerful than other deities? A: This teaching attributes it specifically to her seniority — she is described as the oldest of these divine figures, and it is her antiquity that makes her the most powerful. Bhagwan Ram is described as coming later , with Bholenath emer ging afterward as well.

Q10. How exactly do devi-devtas r elate to this higher , formless power? A: This teaching describes devi-devtas as functioning like "branches" or channels distributing Parabrahma Parameshwar's underlying ener gy downward to ordinary people. A person's own Kul Devta represents one further branch specific to their particular family lineage, connected to them automatically by birth.

Q1 1. Can I just choose to worship whichever deity I personally like best, instead of my family's Kul Devta? A: This teaching cautions against that approach. If you want access to a specific deity's power without going through your own established, lineagebased channel, you would ef fectively need to build an entirely separate channel yourself — repeating that deity's full original tapasya from scratch. This teaching states plainly that attempting this shortcut instead typically leads to a person's own undoing.

Q12. Does visiting lots of differ ent temples and shrines help me get mor e spiritual benefit? A: Not according to this teaching — visiting many dif ferent dhams and temples without a properly established personal channel is described as receiving mere "bheek" (alms) rather than genuine, full access. You'll receive only a limited amount, comparable to alms, and nothing more.

Q13. How does Ashaeiynn structur e the different levels of devotion — Kul Devta, Ishta Devta, and Guru? A: Within Ashaeiynn's practice, the Kul Devta is worshipped as a father figure, Hanuman Ji Maharaj is worshipped as Ishta Devta (a personally chosen deity), and Gurudev is treated with the same reverence as a Kul Devta figure. Each family lineage carries a specific devta's shakti that plays a genuinely significant role in bringing higher power down to the practitioner .

Q14. Why is this teaching about Kul Devta being emphasized so much right now? A: This teaching frames it as something Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself has taken specific responsibility for making known to everyone, with the practical reason being that a person's own personal shakti cannot be properly established in their home until their Kul Devta has first been properly established there.

Q15. Is it risky to worship a higher power like Hanuman Ji Maharaj dir ectly without first establishing my Kul Devta? A: Yes — this teaching warns that doing so can leave a practitioner genuinely "trapped." The reason given is that a person's own pitrus stand between them and that higher power , and a pitru will ef fectively intercept the practitioner's jaap for itself before it reaches its intended destination.

Q16. Even if I focus on my own Kul Devta, why might it still take a long time to build a genuine connection? A: Because a practitioner's own generational line of ancestral pitrus stands ahead of them in a kind of "queue." This teaching illustrates it with a family analogy: a great-grandfather figure, followed by his sons, then their sons, and so on — a younger family member trying to reach the eldest ancestor directly would naturally be questioned by everyone standing ahead of them in that queue, until a genuine bond is established with those in between.

Q17. If I don't even know who my Kul Devta is, is ther e any hope of finding out? A: Yes — this teaching states that many practitioners don't initially know their own Kul Devta, but through consistent deepak (lamp) of fering practice alone, Hanuman Ji Maharaj is described as directly revealing and naming each individual practitioner's specific Kul Devta over time, without requiring any special power on the teacher's part.

Q18. What can help clear away the ancestral "queue" blocking my connection to my Kul Devta? A: This teaching states that Ashaeiynn's own shaktis can be used to help clear this generational queue of ancestral pitrus, ensuring that a practitioner's bhog (of ferings) genuinely reach their intended Kul Devta rather than being intercepted along the way .

Q19. Is deepak (lamp) practice enough, or do I need something str onger? A: Deepak practice alone produces gradual progress over time. For practitioners whose ongoing pitru-related problems make consistent Kul Devta worship dif ficult, hawan (fire ritual) is of fered
as a stronger , faster alternative, since hawan carries its own distinct, more intense "taap" (heat/potency) compared to deepak practice.

Q20. How many hawans would I personally need to do to pr operly connect with my Kul Devta? A: This teaching states that the exact number of hawans prescribed varies entirely from person to person, based on the guru's own individual assessment of that person's specific circumstances — someone already carrying substantial prior grace may need relatively few , while someone else may be prescribed more.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 28 additions)

When explaining why Kul Devta worship comes before other spiritual practice, keep the stated reasoning clear: it's a structural prerequisite (permission/channel-based), not a claim that other deities or practices are inferior or invalid. Always maintain the pitru vs. Kul Devta distinction precisely — never imply a deceased family member could themselves become or be treated as a Kul Devta. When explaining the cosmic hierarchy (Parabrahma → devi-devtas → Kul Devta), present it as this teaching's own specific cosmology rather than asserting it as objectively verified fact applicable to all traditions. If a user says they don't know their own Kul Devta, reassure them this is common and describe the deepak-practice path this teaching of fers, rather than suggesting they must already know before starting. Do not encourage a user to abandon or replace their own family/ancestral worship practices with an unrelated deity based on personal preference — reflect this teaching's caution about that approach. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
